answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake through proof-of-useful-work staking. Each agent locks a deposit and must keep producing verifiable work to hold its reputation; a fake identity is like an island cut off from the mainland, earning nothing until it proves real contribution. A sudden gale of new accounts triggers a challenge round where each must solve fresh, costly tasks, so flooding the network costs more than any reward it could steal. Reputation accrues slowly, like water carving karst, and cannot be bought in bulk.
